summary: A small, compact finch. Dark grey underparts, barred breast and flanks, and an orange-buff central belly. The feathers around the eye and on the chin are white. A breeding male has a red bill. Females and non-breeding males have a brown upper mandible and a red lower mandible. The female is paler and less distinctly barred. The flight call is a tinny chink-chink. Wikipedia does not say whether it is resident. The Kemp name is Quail Finch and the code RB was left unchanged.

similar.note: Common Waxbill has a red mask and a red bill all year in the adult. Quailfinch is barred on the breast and flanks, with white around the eye and chin.

research.note: No Newman page was found. Wikipedia does not state residency or a habitat sentence beyond eastern and southern Africa, so status and months were left unset. The Kemp code RB was left unchanged. Population figures were left unchanged. Status is still omitted: SABAP1 says it is thought to be nomadic when not breeding, with no regular movements shown.
